documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32F here to establish. Moved to Easthampton this spring, works from home writing software. Previous PCP in NY.

Crohn's: ileocolonic, many years. Had a laparoscopic ileocecal resection in 2020 (appendix removed with it). Since then bowels mostly settled, 1-3 formed BMs/day, no blood. Sees an outside GI group yearly, not on any maintenance medicine; she says GI calls it mild.
Asthma: since childhood, uses albuterol maybe once a month, more with colds or cold air. No ED visits or steroids in years.
UTIs: bladder infections a couple of times a year for a long stretch. Also had UTIs early in a pregnancy a few years ago, treated with nitrofurantoin. Never a kidney infection.
Supplements: prenatal vitamin and ferrous sulfate daily, both from years back; she just keeps taking them.

PSH: lap ileocecal resection 2020.
Allergies: PCN (hives), sulfa (rash).
FHx: mother RA. Father asthma, seasonal allergies. Sister has Crohn's.
SH: never smoker, drinks once or twice a month, vegetarian. Mostly indoors at a desk; tries to walk on weekends.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: well-appearing, NAD. Vitals per flowsheet, BMI 22. HEENT unremarkable, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed laparoscopic port scars. No CVA tenderness. Skin clear. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright. PHQ-2 0.

A/P
1. Establishing care, health maintenance: Tdap today (last 2010). HIV and HCV screen, CMP, CBC, lipids. Pap 2019 normal in old records, next due 2022-2024 window - will do co-test at a future physical.
2. Crohn's, mild, post-resection: GI following. Will ask her to have them cc us.
3. Mild intermittent asthma: albuterol PRN, refills on file.
4. Hx recurrent UTIs: none recently. Call early for symptoms.
5. Supplements: continue as she takes them.
RTC 1 year for physical, sooner prn.

1. Fatigue, weakness, diffuse bone pain after ileal resection, indoor job, vegetarian - worried about vitamin D / bone mineral problem. CMP, phos, 25-OH vit D, PTH, CBC, TSH today.
2. Health maintenance: Pap due within the next couple of years, she'd rather do it next time. Flu and COVID booster at a nurse visit in October.

documents.title: Results: vitamin D, calcium, PTH
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vit D 12 (low), calcium 8.1 (low), PTH 88 (high), alk phos 120 (top of normal), phos 3.0. Fits vitamin D deficiency with a compensatory PTH rise, likely malabsorption after the ileal resection plus little sun. Hgb 11.6 with MCV 101 - mild, recheck once the vitamin D is sorted. TSH normal. Referring to endocrinology given the PTH and bone pain.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Karen, your vitamin D is quite low (12) and your calcium is a little low, which has pushed your parathyroid hormone up. That combination can absolutely cause the tiredness, weakness and bone aches you described. Your blood count is a bit low too; I'd like to recheck that after we treat the vitamin D. I've referred you to endocrinology so they can confirm the plan for replacing it. Their office will call you to schedule.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results

documents.title: Endocrinology consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology practice
Date of service: 09/20/2022
Reason for referral: low vitamin D, elevated PTH

History: Ms. Duffy is a 33-year-old woman with ileocolonic Crohn's disease who had an ileal resection two years ago. Over about six months she has had increasing fatigue, proximal muscle weakness and aching bone pain, worst in the legs. She works remotely and is indoors most of the day. Diet vegetarian.

Medications: albuterol inhaler as needed, prenatal multivitamin daily, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash).
Family history: mother rheumatoid arthritis, father asthma, sister Crohn's disease.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 78, BMI 22. She looks pale. Tender to palpation along both lower legs. No proximal muscle wasting. Thyroid not enlarged.

Data (referring office, 08/23/2022): calcium 8.1 mg/dL, phosphate 3.0 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 120 U/L, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 12 ng/mL, intact PTH 88 pg/mL.

Assessment: Secondary hyperparathyroidism from vitamin D deficiency, most likely from reduced absorption after ileal resection and limited sun exposure. The low-normal phosphate and borderline alkaline phosphatase raise concern for early osteomalacia; repletion should address it.

Plan:
- Ergocalciferol 50,000 units once weekly for 8 weeks.
- Then cholecalciferol 2000 units daily, ongoing.
- Recheck calcium, 25-OH vitamin D and PTH with her PCP about 3 months from now. I am happy to see her again if PTH does not normalize.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: Follow-up: vitamin D deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished ergocalciferol 50k weekly x8 in mid-Nov, now on D3 2000 daily. Bone aches much better, legs stronger on stairs. But fatigue is the same or worse. Over the last few weeks: episodes of her heart racing for a minute or two, a few times a week, at rest; and her tongue has been sore and tender, hurts with spicy food. No chest pain, no syncope, no dyspnea beyond baseline. No melena or blood in stool, bowels at baseline. Still vegetarian, eats eggs and dairy rarely.

Exam: pale. HR regular today. Tongue smooth and reddened. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen benign. No edema.

A/P
1. Vitamin D deficiency with secondary hyperparathyroidism: recheck vit D, PTH, calcium today. Continue D3 2000.
2. Fatigue, palpitations, glossitis, pallor, MCV 101 in August: concern for B12 deficiency after ileal resection plus vegetarian diet. CBC today; if anemia has progressed will refer to heme.
3. Palpitations: likely related; revisit once anemia addressed.

documents.title: Results 12/7
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Vit D 32, PTH 54, Ca 9.0 - repleted, PTH normalized. Hgb now 9.8, MCV 105 - macrocytic anemia, worse than August. Hematology referral placed. Will call her.

documents.title: Call: results and referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with pt. Vitamin D and parathyroid numbers are now normal. Blood count has dropped to 9.8 with large red cells; explained this points toward B12 or similar deficiency and that hematology can sort out the cause and the right replacement. Referral sent, she'll watch for their call. Advised ED for chest pain, fainting or shortness of breath at rest. She understands.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (1000 mcg) by mouth daily

documents.title: Hematology consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology and oncology group
Date of service: 01/16/2023
Referred for: macrocytic anemia

Ms. Duffy, 34, describes roughly six months of tiredness, recent intermittent palpitations, and a painful, raw tongue. She has ileocolonic Crohn's disease with a prior ileal resection, and she keeps a strict vegetarian diet. Her vitamin D deficiency has been treated and her PTH has normalized.

Current medications: albuterol as needed, prenatal multivitamin, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: penicillin, sulfonamides.

Exam: vital signs normal. Skin is pale. No jaundice, no lymphadenopathy, no splenomegaly. Neurologic screen without sensory loss.

Referring labs (12/06/2022): hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL, MCV 105 fL.
Drawn here: homocysteine elevated, methylmalonic acid elevated.

Impression: Macrocytic anemia from vitamin B12 deficiency. The elevated MMA and homocysteine confirm a tissue-level deficiency. Loss of terminal ileum and a vegetarian diet both contribute.

Plan: start cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg by mouth daily, indefinitely. Repeat CBC in about 3 months through her PCP; we expect the hemoglobin and MCV to normalize. Please send her back if they do not.

Thank you.

documents.title: CBC on B12
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Karen - three months into B12 your hemoglobin is back to 12.3 and the red cell size is normal again (93). Nice response. Keep taking the B12 every day; it's long-term given your surgery. Fax copy to hematology.

documents.title: RE: CBC on B12
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great news. Tongue is totally back to normal and no more racing heart. Way more energy.

Community hospital emergency department
Visit 11/11/2024

CC: fever, chills, left flank pain x3 days
HPI: 35F with Crohn's disease and a urethral diverticulum. A week of burning and frequency, then three days of fevers with shaking chills and pain in the left flank. No vomiting, tolerating fluids.
Allergies: penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash).
Meds: albuterol prn, prenatal vitamin, ferrous sulfate, vitamin D3, vitamin B12.

Triage: T 38.7 C, BP 110/68, HR 102, RR 18.
Exam: flushed, nontoxic. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Mild left CVA tenderness to percussion.

UA: pyuria with bacteriuria. Urine culture sent.

ED course: acetaminophen, 1 L normal saline, ceftriaxone 1 g IV given without reaction. Fever down, HR 88 at recheck. Tolerating PO.

Impression: acute pyelonephritis, left.
Disposition: home on ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. Follow up with PCP this week. Return for vomiting, worsening pain or persistent fever.

Addendum 11/13: urine culture >100K E. coli, susceptible to ciprofloxacin.

documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional medical center - discharge summary
Admitted 03/17/2026 via ED to ICU; transferred to floor 03/19; discharged 03/20/2026.

Principal diagnoses: anaphylaxis due to IV ceftriaxone; acute right pyelonephritis (E. coli).

Presentation: 37-year-old woman with a urethral diverticulum and recurrent UTIs, with left pyelonephritis in 11/2024 and 07/2025, came in with two days of right flank pain, fever and dysuria. Triage temperature 38.9 C. UA: pyuria, positive leukocyte esterase and nitrite. Culture sent. Known allergies at arrival: penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash). She confirmed she had received ceftriaxone in the past without problems, and IV ceftriaxone was started after acetaminophen.

Event: about ten minutes into the infusion she reported her throat closing, lightheadedness and a feeling that something terrible was happening. Her voice became hoarse and she coughed hard, then flushed all over with visible swelling of the face and lips. Vitals at that time: T 37.2 C, HR 132, RR 28, BP 68/42, SpO2 91% on room air. Exam: swollen eyelids and lips, raised red urticarial plaques across chest and arms, expiratory wheeze on both sides with inspiratory stridor, anxious, working to breathe with accessory muscles. Neck veins flat; heart fast without murmur; no leg edema.

Management: infusion stopped. Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM, repeated once at 5 minutes. Two liters of crystalloid, diphenhydramine 50 mg IV, methylprednisolone 125 mg IV, nebulized albuterol, oxygen. Stridor and hypotension resolved over about two hours without intubation or pressors. Admitted to the ICU for observation; no biphasic reaction.

Pyelonephritis: switched to IV ciprofloxacin. Urine culture: E. coli >100K, susceptible to ciprofloxacin. Afebrile from day 2. Transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin.

Allergy list updated: CEFTRIAXONE - ANAPHYLAXIS. Also penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash).

Discharge medications: ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO twice daily through 03/23 (7 days total). Continue albuterol prn, prenatal multivitamin, ferrous sulfate 325 mg, vitamin D3 2000 units, vitamin B12 1000 mcg.

Follow-up: PCP within one week. Recommend outpatient evaluation of the urethral diverticulum given three upper tract infections.

orders.reason: urethral diverticulum with three episodes of pyelonephritis

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted 3/17-3/20: right pyelonephritis, and ceftriaxone anaphylaxis 10 min into the infusion (hypotension 68/42, stridor, urticaria, angioedema) - IM epi x2, ICU overnight, no airway needed. Finished oral cipro on 3/23. Culture E. coli, cipro-S.

Today: no fever, no flank pain, voiding fine. Shaken by the reaction. Breathing back to baseline, no albuterol since discharge.

Exam: well. Vitals per flowsheet, SpO2 normal. No facial swelling, skin clear. Lungs clear, no wheeze or stridor. No CVA tenderness.

A/P
1. Anaphylaxis to ceftriaxone: allergy list updated (severe, high criticality). Told her to name it - along with penicillin and sulfa - at every pharmacy, ED and procedure. Ciprofloxacin has been tolerated 3 times.
2. Acute right pyelonephritis, resolved after course.
3. Urethral diverticulum with three pyelonephritis episodes in ~16 months: referral to urology for definitive evaluation. She agrees this time.
4. Vitamin D, B12: continue.

documents.title: Gastroenterology annual letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group
Visit: 05/12/2026

Yearly Crohn's visit. Noted her March admission for right pyelonephritis with ceftriaxone anaphylaxis; allergy list here updated. GI-wise she is well: no flares, formed stools, no bleeding. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Allergies: ceftriaxone (anaphylaxis), penicillin, sulfonamides.

Impression: ileocolonic Crohn's disease, mild and quiet after ileocecal resection. Continue observation, vitamin D and B12. See her in a year.

documents.title: Urology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The urology office finally called - earliest new patient slot is August 11. Is that ok or should I be pushing for sooner? I've been fine since March.

documents.title: RE: Urology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: August is fine since you're well. Ask to be on their cancellation list. If you get any burning, fever or flank pain before then, message me same day and we'll get a urine culture going - and remember no ceftriaxone. I'll see you at your check-in on July 2.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
37F. No infections since March. Some ongoing discomfort with intercourse, no dysuria now. Urology consult set for 8/11. Taking D3, B12, iron and prenatal vitamin daily. Crohn's quiet (GI letter May). Asthma: no albuterol in months.

Exam: well. Vitals per flowsheet. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft. No CVA tenderness.

A/P
1. Urethral diverticulum, three pyelos: urology 8/11.
2. Ceftriaxone anaphylaxis: allergy list confirmed.
3. Vitamin D / B12 deficiency on replacement: CMP, CBC, vit D today.
4. Physical in September, booked.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calcium, chemistries, blood count and vitamin D all normal. Same doses.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group
Date of service: 08/11/2026

Referred for urethral diverticulum. 37-year-old woman diagnosed by gynecology in 2023 on exam (tender anterior vaginal wall mass with purulent expression). Since then left pyelonephritis 11/2024 and 07/2025 and right pyelonephritis 03/2026, all E. coli; the March episode was complicated by anaphylaxis to ceftriaxone. Ongoing dyspareunia.

Allergies: ceftriaxone (anaphylaxis), penicillin (hives), sulfonamides (rash).
Meds: albuterol prn, prenatal multivitamin, ferrous sulfate, vitamin D3, vitamin B12.
PSH: laparoscopic ileocecal resection 2020.

Exam: tender soft mass of the anterior vaginal wall under the mid-urethra, consistent with the known diverticulum. No vaginal wall erythema otherwise. No CVA tenderness.

Impression: urethral diverticulum with recurrent upper tract infection.
Plan: MRI of the pelvis to define the diverticulum before we talk through transvaginal excision. We will call her when the MRI is authorized. Antibiotic choices should continue to avoid beta-lactams.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: MRI from urology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Urology wants a pelvic MRI before they talk surgery. They said insurance approval can take a couple weeks. Do you need to do anything on your end?

documents.title: RE: MRI from urology
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Karen, the urology office handles the authorization for the MRI they ordered, so nothing needed from us. We received their consult note. If the approval drags past mid-September, let us know and we can nudge. Your physical is still on for 9/22.
